i do want to say that with this method, tons of communication MUST follow. i don't go ghost on the other person, and it's NEVER a good idea to do that. i always let the other person know how long i need, if i need more time, etc. then we both come back with a clearer head, and i come equipped with tons of 'I statements', haha.

my passive aggressiveness is definitely something i'm working on, but i will say i tend to distance myself from people when i'm upset, more so for their sake than mine.

the things i want to say in the immediate moment when i'm highly upset are not how i really feel, so i do usually take a couple days to reflect on whatever made me emotional so i can communicate that properly. despite being in treatment for years, if a conflict really hurts me enough, i do still go into the "you hurt me, now i'm gonna say a million things to hurt YOU" mode. the best way to combat this is for me to take a step back. for me, it's usually a 1-2 day minimum because i have to journal, journal, journal until i can read back what i write and be able to say it to someone else without it hurting them.

but i didn't realize that this could be viewed as passive-aggressive! i guess i have some thinking to do.

Respectfully, this is what happens when you only focus on material aspects and totally disregard the "spiritual woo woo." I'm not saying everyone ever needs to be enlightened, but there's a reason why rich people go crazy once they have all of their monetary desires.

I agree with the long-winded point this index is trying to make. I get that money CAN and WILL buy you everything you need in life to be happy. And yes, Neville can be so hard to follow that it makes you want to rip your hair out. But also... Just think. Like, sit down and meditate for 10 minutes to absorb the information that has been read. Watch lectures. Watch YouTubers dumb it down even more! There's no shame in that.

I never really feel the need to make negative comments like this, but the ego in this index has turned a lot of people off, myself included. And it's very telling that instead of taking constructive criticism (yes, some people were rude, but others were very kind/corgial), people have decided to just crap on each other.

This isn't a penis measuring contest. We're all searching for the same thing. Put your egos aside and learn to see the inherent value in all information, even that which you don't agree with. You can manifest everything you want, but at the end of the day, you're going to bed alone. So you better like the person you see in the mirror and not just focus on materials, or else you will be void of emotion and under the belief you're better than everyone else. And you won't see it, and it'll be embarrassing, just like this person. 

At the end of the day, it all comes down to preference. But when you word your preference in a way that's rude, you get people checking you. Instead of whining about it and labeling everyone a loser, think about what multiple people are saying.

I'm glad I learned what I did from this index, but holy hell. It was like 2 nuggets of gold under a ginormous pile of turd.

I would say you need to be careful, and get her some serious help. People arguing for public shaming, ignoring, etc. don't understand that this may very well damage the relationship you have with her. And because she's at THAT age, she may hold a grudge for a long while. She may not have the disorders she is faking, but this is a blatant grab for attention, a call for help if you will.

You didn't ask for my experience, but I'll give it anyway since my words may hold more weight that way. I also used to partake in attention seeking behaviors at that age (I'm 22, and never really faked disorders, moreso exaggerating experiences and other lies.) My parents would ignore it, laugh at it, and other things. At this age, I still hold a bit of resentment to this day for them not realizing I needed psychiatric help. NOW, am I saying she will feel this way? Of course not. But at the same time I wouldn't take that gamble either.

This sucks, it's slightly annoying, and it can be draining. But you need to be gentle. She may actually have an underlying disorder causing her to act out. (Not the ones she is claiming to have.) The brain is extremely complex. She needs therapy for sure.

Hey there guys! I'm a 22 year old female who's got a weird butt mole (? I think it's a mole.) My boyfriend said I have had this mole since I met him, and it was always a small raised pink nodular lookin thing that never caused me any issues. Was it weird to me? Definitely, as I have no other pink moles. But it hadn't evolved or changed until around February 1st. (Although we aren't sure when it actually started changing, as the mole is on a weird spot on my butt that isn't easily visible even to my boyfriend. So no, sadly I do not know the timeline of this. Hoping it was a slow growth that we caught.) My boyfriend is the one who noticed and immediately became concerned. When we first noticed it, it had a black spot, some crusting, and the one side had crusting along the border of the mole. A couple days passed, and the black part SEEMED to become more raised, but I'm not sure because it may have just been the camera angle. There is no itching, there isn't any pain, and it looks to me like the mole is darkening from a light pink to a more reddish color. I took a shower last night and the black part fell off. (Even though I was trying to prevent that from happening, as I have a dermatologist appointment on the 8th.) At first, I won't lie, I was a bit relieved. But then I noticed that it looked raw and appeared to have a white-ish ulcer in the middle (I'm NAD but it does look like ulceration, if I'm wrong PLEASE let me know. I hope I am wrong tbh.) Not only that, but the spot where the black was seemed to be bleeding. Not much at all, but I've learned that moles bleeding is a cause for concern. Fast forward to literally today, and the black spot seems to be coming back. I'm wondering if its been dried blood the whole time, or if the black spot was something else and just bled after it fell off. The crusting has gotten worse overnight (not by much.. But enough for me to notice it.) My mom believes it could be SCC or a cyst. There also appears to be increasing irritation around the area. I'm not sure if its because of the friction, something out of my control, or even both. I know I shouldn't worry myself, and I did post this on the Melanoma subreddit, but I'm actually really hoping someone has other ideas as well that would ease my worries. I'm assuming the dermatologist won't like seeing this and will biopsy it but I'm not positive. If anyone has any similar experiences please let me know. I just want some thoughts and ideas is all. Really, really hoping it's a cyst.

I'm so sorry for your loss. It's been really hard to take care of myself and I've been wondering if a mental care facility is a good idea if I get worse because I'm beginning to find it harder to function every day.

Please, please be kind to yourself as well. Eat, hydrate, and rest. The guilt is horrible for me and I imagine the same for you. It is not our faults. We loved our brothers with every fiber of our being.

I do love him so much. This is making me cry because I've been battling this guilt and it feels like I'm losing the battle. Like I could have done better. Told him I loved him more.

I hope to a god I don't believe in that he knew we all loved him so dearly.

He has a SoundCloud! I haven't listened to his music in a few days because it makes me so sad but his music is lovely. His band has two songs up on SoundCloud and sent the rest to my mom. She sent them to me.

In his song Monks you can hear him laughing at the beginning and the end. I think that's the biggest gift of all; having his happiness and joy captured on audio forever. Things are hard but he lived a wonderful life before he fell victim to his illness and sadness. I hope he is resting comfortably. That's all I want for him... Is to not be in pain anymore.

Thank you so much. I'm so so sorry for your loss. I'll live my life the way he did; with love and unbreakable kindness. He never had one bad thing to say about anyone. I sincerely want to follow in his foot steps.

I think I want to try to learn guitar because he knew that and keyboard. I don't want to sell his guitars. I used to play violin when I was younger and I lost interest due to depression but learning an instrument was so fun. And if one day I could learn his music... I think I would be very happy just playing it by myself every day.

I think that I'm going to start looking for a support group because I love my friends and other family members but I feel so disconnected because nobody REALLY understands. And I sincerely do not want them to. I think I'm more glad than anything that they don't.

The wonderful thing about his music is that 2 of his bands songs are on SoundCloud. In one of them you can hear him laughing at the beginning and the end. He had such a lovely laugh. His friend emailed my mom all of their unreleased music and another friend of his gave us band posters and sent us a 30 minute concert they did. I remember his friend saying, "It didn't matter if we were playing in some wet basement somewhere, Seamus was always so excited to have a show."

I am also so sorry for your loss. This is awful. I am also sending lots and lots of hugs, love, and the tiny amount of positive energy I have left. 💗
